mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three months, contradicting the predicted negative direction.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the joint proxy condition fails to precede negative returns in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals labor market softness masked by falling participation, which reduces wage growth and corporate margin potential, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger condition fails to precede negative returns in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the INDPRO decline fails to precede negative returns in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above 10% year-over-year indicates a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the HOUST YoY condition fails to precede positive returns in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a period of elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 6%) signals an emergency easing response, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.5pp in one month AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 6%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint trigger condition fails to precede positive returns in at least 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, which compresses margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the UNRATE trigger fails to precede negative returns in at least 65% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) of more than 3% with a concurrent rise in the savings rate (RSAFS) above 7% signals reduced consumer spending power and precautionary saving, which depresses consumption-sensitive sectors and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint GDPC1/RSAFS trigger fails to precede negative returns in at least 70% of cases.
